blockers.quote: You walk past six people and say it: five copies, please, because I need to make copies.
blockers.why: Check #7 Misconception first: you ask an employee to perform a routine service, while the six people whose place you take are never asked. The stranger-compliance fact therefore does not break the wrong belief through the action shown.
blockers.fix: Make the first student in the queue the target: “You ask the first student to let you go ahead for five copies, because you need to make copies.” Show that student step aside; only then does the clerk take the folder.

suggestions.quote: Psychologists count it as a basic need, next to feeling capable and feeling close to people. Choosing for yourself. (c10)
suggestions.fix: Move this before line 209, so the fact loads the idea and “A no was the only thing...” delivers the turn instead of the story pausing after its conclusion.

suggestions.quote: So you stop asking. Statements. Silences. And you find out how much of talking to someone was asking them things.
suggestions.fix: After this, show you type “Ask Ma for me?” to Dev, then delete it; this acknowledges the intermediary loophole while keeping the question something you must risk asking yourself.

suggestions.quote: In Milgram's study, 65% of the men went all the way to the last switch. (c06, c07)
suggestions.fix: Cut this spoken statistic; retain the drawn dial, the fake-shock clarification and “please continue,” then move directly to recognizing your own voice.

keep.quote: Every yes is the same yes now. So you stop looking at faces.
He remembers agreeing. He can't remember wanting to.
The chance of being told no. Which is the only way anyone has ever told you the truth.
